$comment: MACHINE half of the /openai/v1/chat/completions + /openai/v1/models contract; the HUMAN half is openai-chat.md. The gateway inspects only what is declared here; the OpenAI Chat body is the vendor's and streams through byte-unchanged. `upstream` declares per rail the URL and credential header the fake upstream must receive. Cross-cutting requirement IDs here resolve to their one heading on anthropic-messages.md / sessions.md (rule 7).

authorization.description: the session token as a bearer — consulted first

x-api-key.description: the session token for SDKs that send x-api-key

x-opencode-session.description: the Go rail's native session id — passthrough

body.description: an OpenAI Chat Completions request; only `model` and `stream` are read

model.description: must name the session's model as the harness spells it (the wire id); absent = filled

upstream.$comment: per rail: what the fake upstream must receive for POST chat/completions. Credential placeholders name the Secret key, never a value.

models.$comment: GET /openai/v1/models — a passthrough on the rails that have one.

output.description: the upstream response, status + headers (minus hop-by-hop) + body bytes, relayed unchanged; `retry-after` kept on 429

complete.description: a 2xx is complete when a non-streamed body was read to its end, or a stream carried its terminal event; otherwise the request row's `incomplete` names the reason

session-unknown.description: no session token, or a token no row's hash matches

session-released.description: the session was released by DELETE /sessions/{id}

credential-unresolved.description: the session's rail credential is a definitive miss

credential-transient.description: the kube API failed or was unreachable while resolving the session's credential; retry

model-not-session.description: the body's model is not the session's model

dialect-unsupported-on-rail.description: the session's rail does not speak the openai dialect (the anthropic rail)

upstream-auth.description: the upstream answered 401, or 403 naming a credential reason — the rail credential is bad (marked rejected for admission); 4xx so no harness retries it; the upstream body is never relayed

upstream-refused.description: a 403 that names no credential reason — a policy refusal of this model/request; the credential is untouched; the body is never relayed

upstream-unreachable.description: the upstream connection failed for a reason that is not a timeout (DNS, refused, TLS, reset); nothing reached the vendor

header-refused.description: a credential-shaped value in a header the gateway does not own — refused before any upstream call (the FU-251 tripwire)
